source.title: T-MARS: Improving Visual Representations by Circumventing Text Feature Learning
source.authors: Pratyush Maini; Sachin Goyal; Zachary Chase Lipton; J. Kolter; Aditi Raghunathan

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream performance scaling in CLIP-style vision-language models, an extension beyond language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure held-out language-model cross-entropy, vary parameter count, or fit or test loss power laws. It does report zero-shot ImageNet accuracy for fixed architectures trained on LAION pools from 2M to 64M, with training compute scaled proportionally to pool size; these results bear on V6. Other reported filtering comparisons and the synthetic data-utility experiments do not test the listed scaling-law versions.
record.test_reason: This is a data-filtering method paper for CLIP-style models. Its 'scaling trends' (Fig. 1b, 3a; Table 5) report the zero-shot accuracy gain of T-MARS over unfiltered LAION as pool size and compute grow together. That is the study's own method compared with a baseline, not a test of how loss or downstream performance scales. No power law is fitted, parameter count is not varied, and no loss is reported. Scaling laws appear only in related work (Appendix B). The absolute accuracy series does rise with data and compute, but it is a vision-language setting with confounded data and compute and no fitted law. It is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test of V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that T-MARS, which masks text and re-scores CLIP similarity to drop text-dominated images, beats filtering baselines on LAION subsets and DataComp. They report that its accuracy gains over no filtering grow roughly linearly as data and compute scale exponentially. They also argue that removing bad examples has about 3× the utility of adding good ones.
record.recipe_differences: This is CLIP-style vision-language training with data filtering and zero-shot accuracy evaluation, not language-model loss scaling or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Pool size/data scale; training compute was kept proportional to pool size. The reported study also compares filtering strategies, but this record's rows capture the T-MARS scaling series.

fits_no_version.finding: For CLIP-style ResNet-50 and ViT-B-32 models on LAION subsets from 2M to 64M, with compute equal to pool size, the zero-shot ImageNet gain of T-MARS over unfiltered LAION grows roughly linearly in log pool size. For ResNet-50 the gain goes from about 0.9 to 6.1 points. Unfiltered LAION accuracy also rises monotonically (ResNet-50: 2.57 → 26.34).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-quality filtering gains for contrastive vision-language models grow roughly log-linearly as data and compute are scaled together; curation can shift the data-scaling curve upward.

record.problems: The reported LAION scaling accuracies have no uncertainty estimates stated. The scaling experiment changes the training data-pool size and proportional compute while keeping architecture fixed, so it does not establish language-model loss scaling or scaling with parameter count.
record.rows_left_out: Other filtering methods and the 16M/32M/64M repeated table entries are not separately included; the rows focus on the T-MARS 2M–64M ImageNet accuracy series from Appendix E, Table 5. Results on other benchmark metrics and DataComp are not this scale-series measure.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss measured, no power-law fit in parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-run fits extrapolated to larger runs.
Two architectures (ResNet-50, ViT-B-32) are compared, but not at matched parameter counts, and no shape sweep.
Vision-language setting, but no power-law form is fitted to loss or error.

Accuracy rises with jointly scaled data and compute, but there is no predictive fit, no relation to pretraining loss, and no separation of data from compute. The scaling claim concerns the filtering gain, not performance itself.
No comparison of exponents or fitting choices. Data curation altering scaling is mentioned only via Sorscher et al. in related work.

record.verdict_notes: Relation and tranche are changed from the reader's tests/T3 to discusses/T6. The scaling experiment evaluates the filtering method's gain, not a scaling law. Table 5's column layout was likely misread for the ViT-B-32 rows: the reader's ViT 'ImageNet' values match the seventh column (likely ViT VTAB). The rows_left_out claim of '16M/32M/64M repeated table entries' refers to Table 1 duplicating Table 5, which is fine. No uncertainty estimates are given for the LAION runs.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model loss or parameter, token, or compute loss scaling is measured.
No small-run loss fits or predictions of larger-run loss are reported.
No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is measured.
No architecture comparison at fixed parameter count is reported.
The paper studies vision-language models and varies data-pool size, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds for loss in another modality or training regime.
Tests zero-shot ImageNet accuracy against data-pool scale for two fixed vision-language architectures, not language-model downstream performance or performance as a function of pretraining loss.
No comparison of scaling-law exponents or fit choices, and no claim about curves bending away from a power law.
